definition: The use of AI models to automatically generate test cases for a given piece of software, aiming to improve test coverage and catch edge cases.
details: AI-driven test generation can help identify edge cases a human tester might overlook and reduce the manual effort required to build comprehensive test suites, particularly for large or rapidly changing codebases.

explainer.lead: Test case generation uses AI models to automatically generate test cases for software. It matters because it can improve test coverage and catch edge cases, especially in large or fast-changing codebases.

tiers.eli5: Instead of a person writing every test by hand, an AI writes tests for the program, including tricky situations a human might forget.
tiers.practitioner: Teams use it to reduce manual effort in building comprehensive test suites and to surface edge cases a human tester might overlook. The facts here do not describe specific pitfalls.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as the use of AI models to automatically generate test cases for a given piece of software, aiming to improve test coverage and catch edge cases; no formal metric is given here.

explainer.example: For a large, rapidly changing codebase, an AI generates candidate test cases covering inputs a manual tester had not considered.
